question: What is the nature of washing soda?
solution: The correct answer is __**Basic**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • **Washing soda** (sodium carbonate, Na₂CO₃) is a basic compound. • When dissolved in water, **it produces hydroxide ions (OH⁻), making the solution alkaline.** • **This basic nature is why it is used in cleaning agents to neutralize acidic substances and remove grease or oil.** • **Washing soda is a water-softening agent** because it reacts with the calcium and magnesium ions in hard water to form insoluble precipitates, thereby removing hardness from the water. • This property** enhances its effectiveness in cleaning.**
